Saying: God said it, I believe it, that settles it
WhatItMeans: The speaker is declaring full confidence in Scripture — if God said it, that is the end of the argument, whatever anyone else thinks.
WhatTheBibleSays: God's word is indeed settled: "For ever, O LORD, thy word is settled in heaven" (Psalm 119:89), and all Scripture is given by inspiration of God (2 Timothy 3:16). But notice the order in the slogan — God said it, I believe it, that settles it — as if God's word waits on my belief to become settled. My position is that the slogan gets the order wrong: God's word is settled whether I believe it or not, and my belief is the response, not the seal. The sentiment is sound; the wording puts me in the middle where I do not belong.
Origin: No single author is documented. The phrase was popularised in the 1970s — the Heritage Singers published the song "God Said It, I Believe It" in 1975 and filmed a music video for it in 1976 — and it circulated widely as a bumper sticker. Billy Graham is sometimes associated with it, but there is no evidence he coined it.
Sources: Heritage Singers, "God Said It, I Believe It" (1975); on-site KJV text of Psalm 119:89 and 2 Timothy 3:16
